goal: Restate the two inverted guardrails so each fails on the regression it names instead of on a spelling: the unattended worktree prohibition becomes an assertion over the Git argument vectors the batch runtime can actually produce, and the v3-island coverage assertion becomes an assertion that production code imports none of the retired plan_core exports.

acceptance.assertion: The worktree guard in tests/unattended-contracts.test.ts no longer regex-matches source text. It asserts that no Git argument vector the batch runtime can produce begins with `worktree`, so an invocation assembled through a variable, template literal, or helper is caught, and a legitimate mention of the word in a reason key or comment no longer fails the suite. The prohibition itself is unchanged: batch execution still creates, switches, and deletes no Git worktree.

The `retains coverage for the surviving runtime modules` assertion in tests/v3-island-deletion.test.ts stops requiring that a named test file contain a module path substring. It asserts instead that production code imports none of the retired plan_core exports, which is the property the substring stood in for, so retiring a dead test or renaming a module no longer reads as guardrail weakening.

Neither guard is removed and neither protected property is weakened: both suites still fail when the prohibited behavior is reintroduced, and the full unattended and island suites pass unchanged otherwise.
